1: Candidates were asked to select the task which would not be performed by a book-keeper. The correct answer is A. Most candidates answered correctly.
4: Candidates were presented with a ledger account and were required to select the correct statement about this account. The correct answer is B. Rami is a supplier and Peter has received cash discount from him for paying early. Some candidates thought that Rami had received a discount for buying in bulk. However, discounts for buying in bulk are not recorded in the ledger accounts.
6: Candidates were asked to identify the book of prime entry in which goods bought on credit are recorded. The correct answer is C. Candidates seemed to find this question straightforward, and most answered correctly.
9: This question covered the topic of correction of errors. Candidates were asked to calculate the effect on profit, of correcting two stated errors. The correct answer was D. Although there were many correct answers, some candidates found this question challenging.
10: This question asked candidates to identify the journal entry required to correct the stated error. Fatima’s account had been debited with $450 in error, so that account needs to be credited with $900 (i.e., $450 to cancel the incorrect entry and another $450 to make the correct entry). Some candidates found this question challenging. The correct answer is D.
11: Candidates were required to adjust the bank statement balance in order to arrive at the updated cash book balance. The correct answer is A. $740 – $150 = $590. Some candidates calculated the original cash book balance (i.e., the balance before the bank charges are deducted to arrive at the updated balance) and so they selected B as their answer. Other candidates added the unpresented cheques to the bank statement balance and deducted the bank charges, and arrived at $860 which was option C.
12: This question covered the topic of control accounts. It asked what information is obtained from the general journal in order to prepare the purchases ledger control account. The correct answer is A. While many candidates answered correctly, a significant number of candidates thought that goods returned to suppliers were recorded in the general journal.
15: Candidates were required to calculate the balance on a provision for depreciation account. The correct answer is A. The calculation is ([$35 000 – $12 600]  20%) + $12 600 = $17 080. Some candidates calculated the balance on the provision at the start of the year instead of at the end of the year.
16: This question covered the topic of income received in advance and income received in arrears. The correct answer is A. The calculation is $8650 – $600 – $7900 = $150 in advance, i.e., on the credit side. Some candidates found this challenging.
17: Candidates were required to calculate the change in the balance on a provision for doubtful debts account. Most candidates correctly calculated this as $10, but some thought that this represented a debit to the provision rather than a credit. The correct answer is B.
19: Question 22 Candidates were required to select an advantage to a sole trader of forming a partnership. The correct answer is D. Most candidates found this question to be straightforward and answered correctly.
23: This question asked candidates to identify correct statements in relation to the financial statements of a partnership. The correct answer is B. Some candidates thought that partners’ salaries are shown as an expense in the income statement.
27: Candidates were asked to calculate the profit or loss for the year, from changes in capital over time. The correct answer is D. The calculation is $25 000 + $5000 = $30 000 profit. Some candidates subtracted the decrease in liabilities from the increase in assets, instead of adding it.
28: This question covered the topic of incomplete records. Candidates were required to select the option which showed how profit for the year may be calculated. The correct answer is B. Some candidates found this question challenging.
29: Candidates were required to calculate the sales total by adding together the figures for cash payments, cash drawings, cash banked and cash in hand. The correct answer is D. Some candidates deducted the payments and drawings instead of adding them.
30: This question required candidates firstly to use the mark-up of 25% to calculate cost of sales, and then to use that figure to calculate purchases for the year. The correct answer is D. Some candidates found this calculation challenging.
31: This question covered trade payables turnover. The correct answer is C. The calculation is (8000/[150 000 – 17 000])  365 = 22 days. Although there were many correct answers, some candidates did not use the formula correctly, or used an incorrect figure for credit purchases.
